companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The insurer and health services company had a relatively slow year for revenue growth, but profits, at $6.7 billion, were up 24.3%.

  • Cigna has been working to expand “value-based” care models, which are designed to emphasize primary care and preventive medicine. To strengthen such care, Cigna entered into a strategic partnership with Walgreens-owned primary care provider VillageMD.

  • Evernorth, Cigna’s service-provider arm, which also oversees the new VillageMD investment, has brought the company growth over recent years, and focuses on value-based care.

  • Cigna Healthcare, the health-insurance benefits arm of the business, also expanded its margins and customer base.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Global health services company Cigna had an up-and-down year. Despite bringing on an additional 8.4 million customers in its pharmacy division in 2021 and an 8.5% rise in sales, Cigna’s profits plummeted by 36% from 2020, to $5.37 billion. After years of litigation, an appeals court rejected Cigna’s attempt to claim a $1.85 billion breakup fee from Anthem in the wake of a merger agreement that fell apart a few years ago.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: If there’s one element you need to home in on to understand health insurer Cigna’s 2020 success, Evernorth is a pretty good place to start. The company climbed more than 50 spots on the Fortune 500 after completing its merger with pharmacy benefits manager Express Scripts. That sent its revenues skyrocketing—and then the pandemic hit. How did Cigna manage to deal with that buzz saw? The Evernorth subsidiary, which encompasses Express Scripts, brought in $30.6 billion in the first quarter of 2021 and moved to expand its plan memberships in five more states and 67 new counties. It doesn’t hurt that Evernorth acquired the virtual care platform MDLive at the beginning of 2021—at a time when telehealth demand is soaring.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Health insurer Cigna is enjoying a meteoric rise on the Global 500 this year, climbing 197 spots thanks to its merger with pharmacy benefits giant Express Scripts—yet another example of the trend toward "vertical integration" among large health care companies. The Express Scripts integration, completed in December 2018, fueled revenue growth that exceeded even Cigna’s own pre-merger expectations: Adjusted revenues for 2019 soared to $140 billion, compared with the $131 billion to $133 billion originally forecast.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
